liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Comes A Time** (4 reviews): Reviewer calls this the best Comes A Time they've heard, within the Playin' > Comes A Time > Playin' > Around And Around > Alabama run; Described as a dynamite version of Comes A Time [14][16][19][22]
- **Mississippi Half-Step Uptown Toodeloo** (2 reviews): Reviewer counts this Half Step among the best they've heard; Reviewer says the opening Half Step started a little rough but improved [15][22]
- **Row Jimmy** (1 review): The whistling continues during Row Jimmy, while Weir is learning slide guitar [18]
- **Feel Like A Stranger** (1 review): The second half of Feel Like A Stranger has a nice extended jam [17]
- **Little Red Rooster** (1 review): DeadBase reportedly lists this as the first Little Red Rooster the Dead played [17]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Reviewer singles out the China Cat > Rider sequence as a favorite part of the show [19]
- **Alabama Getaway** (1 review): Reviewer hears the highest-energy Alabama Getaway they know, a surprise after Around And Around, where they expected Good Lovin' [21]

## Setlist highlights

- Earliest performances in the archive: Little Red Rooster [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-08-19.174765.sbd.88172.remaster.miller.flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 24 songs; 185 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1980-08-19.sbd.miller.88172.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 24 songs; 184 min; rated 3.5/5 by 8 [2]. Said about its sound: The soundboard is a big improvement over the clappy balcony audience recordings; Soundboard has spotty sound quality and cuts in and out; Uploader warns that the soundboard is poor quality, though the show itself is great [2][19][21]
- **gd80-08-19.naks.munder.8739.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 24 songs; 186 min; rated 4.16/5 by 19 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience-heavy recording, yet the band stays clear in the mix and it conveys the feeling of being present; Recording quality disappoints the reviewer, who believes a better audience tape exists somewhere; Fair balcony audience recording with distant vocals, but the balance improves nicely across Playin' > Comes A Time > Playin' [12][14][16][18]
- **gd1980-08-19.151796.aud.flac1644**: audience recording; 24 songs; 178 min [4]

## Around the show

- The crowd is audibly ecstatic throughout the recording [12]
- The crowd's reaction during the China Cat > Rider pairing is worth listening to [15]
- Reviewer attended, left early after drinking too much beer, and recalls the Uptown as amazing [20]
- Show was sold out; police chased away the reviewer, who was trying to get in without a ticket [22]
- The Mississippi River Festival show from the same year is also called good [15]
- Setlist is unusual for this period of the band's history [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-08-19.174765.sbd.88172.remaster.miller.flac1644**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  October 23, 2025; source: Set 1: SBD > Cassette Master > ? > Cassette Set 2: SBD > Cassette Master > Cassette > Reel > DAT [1]. Also: Remaster of shnid 88172 with the soundboard's vocal phase issue fixed and all sources pitch corrected; Patch source was recorded by Dougal Donaldson [1]
- **gd1980-08-19.sbd.miller.88172.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Set 1: SBD -> Cassette Master -> ? -> Cassette ; Set 2: SBD -> Cassette Master -> ? -> Dat (48k) [2]. Also: Soundboard patched with a Nakamichi 700 cassette master source (shnid 8739) for Half-Step, Stranger, Eyes and Playing In The Band [2]
- **gd80-08-19.naks.munder.8739.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording: Nak 700's w/shotgun caps [3]. Also: Balcony recording with Nakamichi 700s and shotgun capsules, to Sony TC-158 cassette, DAT, CD; via Mark Lindenbaum, seeded by Willy [3]
- **gd1980-08-19.151796.aud.flac1644**: taped by tapes from the collection of Brian Schley.; transferred by Transferred by Andrew F. 02/2021; source: Source: Sennheiser MD-421's (1st row balcony) > TC-D5 > MAC > Low-Gen (1st or 2nd) tapes from the collection of Brian Schley. [4]. Also: Second set has patches from ID 8739 covering gaps and spots of tape damage [4]
